changes: Normalized the surname title: 'tṛpāṭhī' is kept as written and 'tripāṭhī' is added as the standard form.
Added a note that 'paramārtham' may be a corruption of 'parārtham'; it is kept as written in purpose.
Checked the date: ŚS 1732 + 78 = 1810 CE. Āṣāḍha śukla 12 falls around June–July 1810, which matches the catalogue's ŚS 1732.
Kept the weekday as written ('bhṛśau'), with the note that it is probably 'bhṛgau', meaning Friday.

purpose: paramārtham (possibly for parārtham: copied for someone else)
notes: 'bhṛśau' is probably a scribal error for 'bhṛgau' (Friday). 'tṛpāṭhī' is the surname Tripāṭhī, so it goes in titles. 'dvijavara' is an epithet meaning 'best of brahmins'. 'paramārtham' may be a mistake for 'parārtham' ('for another'); if so, the copy was made for someone else, who is not named. The text belongs to the Pañcastavī; no author is named in the colophon.
